headline_marked: 7 [[seven top Awami League leaders sentenced to death]] for July atrocities
headline: 7 seven top Awami League leaders sentenced to death for July atrocities
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal has ordered the execution of seven leaders from the banned Awami League and its associate organizations for crimes against humanity during the July uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced seven top leaders of the banned Awami League and its affiliate organizations to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.
The convicted leaders include high-ranking members of the Awami League, Jubo League, and Chhatra League.
The tribunal's verdict has been hailed by the families of the victims of the July atrocities, who are seeking swift execution of the sentence.
In a significant move, the court has ordered that half of the assets of five of the convicted leaders be sold to compensate the victims.
Approximately Tk 22.5 crore of declared assets from four of the leaders will be used to provide financial support to the victims and their families.
The ruling marks a major legal milestone in seeking justice for the victims of the July uprising.
caption:
Seven top Awami League leaders have been sentenced to death for crimes against humanity during the July uprising.

The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced seven top leaders of the banned Awami League and its affiliate organizations to death for crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising.

The convicted leaders include high-ranking members of the Awami League, Jubo League, and Chhatra League.

The tribunal's verdict has been hailed by the families of the victims of the July atrocities, who are seeking swift execution of the sentence.

In a significant move, the court has ordered that half of the assets of five of the convicted leaders be sold to compensate the victims.

Approximately Tk 22.5 crore of declared assets from four of the leaders will be used to provide financial support to the victims and their families.

The ruling marks a major legal milestone in seeking justice for the victims of the July uprising.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: Multiple [[crude bomb blasts hit Dhaka]] in separate incidents
headline: Multiple crude bomb blasts hit Dhaka in separate incidents
summary: Three explosions occurred near Dhaka University and one in front of the Supreme Court following a high-profile tribunal verdict.
details: Three crude bomb explosions were reported in the Dhaka University area around 10:45 PM. Two blasts occurred in front of Jagannath Hall and one near the TSC Metro Rail station.
No casualties were immediately reported in the university area. Dhaka University Proctor Israfil Ratan confirmed that police and assistant proctors are investigating the incidents.

Earlier in the day, a crude bomb exploded in front of the main gate of the Supreme Court. This incident followed a verdict by the International Crimes Tribunal-2, which sentenced seven defendants, including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Kader, to death for crimes against humanity during the July uprising.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that CCTV footage has helped identify two suspects in the Supreme Court blast. He suggested the perpetrators might be miscreants associated with the Awami League and confirmed that a government investigation is underway.
caption:
Four crude bomb blasts rocked Dhaka in a single day, targeting the Supreme Court and Dhaka University areas.

Three crude bomb explosions were reported in the Dhaka University area around 10:45 PM. Two blasts occurred in front of Jagannath Hall and one near the TSC Metro Rail station.

No casualties were immediately reported in the university area. Dhaka University Proctor Israfil Ratan confirmed that police and assistant proctors are investigating the incidents.

Earlier in the day, a crude bomb exploded in front of the main gate of the Supreme Court. This incident followed a verdict by the International Crimes Tribunal-2, which sentenced seven defendants, including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Kader, to death for crimes against humanity during the July uprising.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that CCTV footage has helped identify two suspects in the Supreme Court blast. He suggested the perpetrators might be miscreants associated with the Awami League and confirmed that a government investigation is underway.

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV
